note: Clean pass with disclosures. 195 rows = 39 items x 5 response levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes on both sets (FFMQ_1..FFMQ_39, resp 1-5). (1) MAPPING IS LABEL-TIED, NOT INFERRED, AND EXEMPT UNDER STEP 5b. data/PEMAIW_Qiu_2020.R does select(starts_with('FFMQ')) then pivot_longer(names_to='item'), so the IRW item code IS the source column name verbatim (code-derivation pattern 1, core model s3) -- no positional slice, no renumbering. The source is a Qualtrics export whose second row carries the full administered question text per column, so code and wording are tied at the source: mapping_basis=data_labels, and Step 5b's exemption is earned by the derivation, not merely claimed. Both recruitment files were checked and their 39 label strings are byte-identical to each other. (2) CORROBORATED AGAINST THE LIVE DATA ANYWAY. Per-item non-missing counts computed from the two OSF CSVs (respondents only, i.e. after dropping the two Qualtrics metadata rows, as the IRW script does) reproduce irw_table_sets() per-item n for all 39 items exactly, 0 mismatches (e.g. FFMQ_1 1174, FFMQ_10 1180, FFMQ_19 1175, FFMQ_39 1174; total 45854 non-missing of 46176 rows). Only 10 distinct n values occur, so this does not by itself distinguish every item from every other -- the column-name identity does. No separate verification sidecar is written because mapping_basis is data_labels. (3) TRANSCRIPTION IS LITERAL, INCLUDING THE STUDY'S OWN TYPOS. item_text is the administered Qualtrics wording verbatim, so it keeps 'deliberatey' (FFMQ_1), 'beliefs, opinions and expectations' (FFMQ_7, canonical has 'opinions, and'), 'I make judgement about' (FFMQ_17, canonical 'judgments'), and 'distressing thoughts or image' (FFMQ_24, canonical 'images'). Canonical Baer et al. wording was deliberately NOT substituted. Only the shared Qualtrics prefix was removed from each label: every label reads '<instructions> - <item>', and that prefix is shipped once in instructions. (4) OPTIONS COME FROM THE STUDY'S OWN MATERIALS AND CARRY EXPLICIT NUMBERS. materials_survey.pdf's FFMQ block prints the administered anchors with their codes -- 'never or very rarely true (1)', 'rarely true (2)', 'sometimes true (3)', 'often true (4)', 'very often or always true (5)' -- matching materials_FFMQ39.pdf's 1-5 scale, and the raw CSV columns already store integers 1-5, so resp is used (not raw_resp) and the option axis needs no inference either. No item is stored reverse-scored: the raw values are the as-administered 1-5 responses and the FFMQ's R-keyed items (12,16,22 and the Act-with-Awareness and Nonjudge blocks) are reversed only at scoring time, which the IRW table does not do. (5) SHAPE. instructions holds the single whole-instrument prompt (identical for every item); section_id is the trivial single value with a blank section_prompt; correct_response NA (no key, so key_source is empty); language column omitted (administered in English, Western University / online North American recruitment). (6) RIGHTS: no block. The FFMQ is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. No clause reserving a fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution right could be found or quoted for the FFMQ: the study's own materials_FFMQ39.pdf carries description, items, scoring key and the Baer et al. (2006) reference and no terms of use at all; Ruth Baer's Oxford publication page (psych.ox.ac.uk/team/ruth-baer/publication_modal/2348143) is CloudFront-403 to a plain fetch and to a browser UA, so no statement could be read there; the only third-party characterisations locatable are permissive and hedged -- positivepsychology.com states 'This scale is freely available to use', and db.arabpsychology.com states it is 'frequently utilized in non-commercial academic research and clinical practice, generally available without an associated fee for these uses. Users should always consult the primary authors for specific permissions related to commercial applications or large-scale projects.' That last sentence is a third-party aggregator's summary, not the rights holder's own terms, and is recorded here rather than treated as a quotable restriction; under irw#1945 silence at the originator is permission. Millisecond's 'Included with an Inquisit license' is a term of Millisecond's software, not of the instrument. Absence of a retrievable clause is not absence of a clause -- this records what was checked. FFMQ was NOT added to instrument_rights_register.csv by this agent to avoid a write race with the sibling PEMAIW_Qiu_2020_DASS agent; a register row (verdict=ship) is worth adding at round close. (7) STEP 3b: instrument confirmed. Live data is 39 items on 1-5, which is the full FFMQ-39 and matches materials_FFMQ39.pdf item for item; the same deposit's other instruments (DASS-21, MEQ-30, MLQ-10, PANAS-20, BWSS-20, SWLS-5) are separate IRW tables and none of their columns appear here. source_ref: Pellerin N, Raufaste E (2020) 'Psychological Resources Protect Well-Being During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Longitudinal Study During the French Lockdown', Frontiers in Psychology 11:590276, doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2020.590276 (CC BY 4.0; PMC7793808). DATA: OSF project https://osf.io/45aq3/, file data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv (https://osf.io/download/dc6me/). Processing script: data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py. ITEM TEXT: Lorenz T, Beer C, Puetz J, Heinitz K (2016) 'Measuring Psychological Capital: Construction and Validation of the Compound PsyCap Scale (CPC-12)', PLOS ONE 11(4):e0152892, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0152892 (CC BY 4.0), S1 Appendix (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0152892.s001), which prints the CPC-12 in German and English with each item annotated by its parent scale; self-efficacy is items 10-12 (GSE4, GSE10, GSE6). VERIFICATION DATA: the same article's S2 Dataset (.s002, n=321) and S3 Dataset (.s003, n=202). RESPONSE ANCHORS: Pellerin & Raufaste Materials section. RIGHTS: General Self-Efficacy Scale FAQ, https://userpage.fu-berlin.de/~health/faq_gse.pdf. Sources cached under itemtext/.cache/pellerin2020_cpc_selfefficacy/.
note: PASS WITH CAVEATS. 21 rows = 3 items x 7 response levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes on both sets (SAE_1/SAE_2/SAE_3; resp 1-7; live table 3,030 rows, per-item n=1,010). (1) INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): the live data is the 3-item self-efficacy facet of the CPC-12 (Lorenz, Beer, Puetz & Heinitz 2016, PLOS ONE 11(4):e0152892). Confirmed three ways: data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py melts exactly ['SAE_1','SAE_2','SAE_3']; Pellerin & Raufaste (2020) write that they assessed 'self-efficacy (e.g., "I am confident that I could deal efficiently with unexpected events") using the Compound-Psychological-Capital questionnaire (CPC-12, Lorenz et al., 2016)', and that quoted example is CPC-12 item 10 verbatim; and the live 1-7 range matches the paper's stated uniform 1='strongly disagree' to 7='strongly agree' format. The CPC-12's resilience facet was not administered. No mismatch. (2) TEXT SOURCE: the OSF deposit (osf.io/45aq3) holds only PsyR_lockdown2020.R and data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv; the CSV header carries bare codes (SAE_1..SAE_3, Hope_1.., Opt_1..) and no variable or value labels, and the R file is an analysis script with no item strings. The Frontiers article has no supplementary material and prints one example item per scale. So the wording ships from the instrument's own publication: the CPC-12 S1 Appendix (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0152892.s001, CC BY 4.0), whose self-efficacy block is items 10-12, transcribed verbatim including terminal full stops. Those three are the General Self-Efficacy Scale's German items 4, 10 and 6 (the appendix marks them GSE4/GSE10/GSE6). (3) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: the study was run in France in French. The administered French wording is not recoverable in scope - it is in neither the OSF deposit (both files checked) nor the article or its supplements (there are none). So this takes the documented fallback: English in the base fields, _translated columns omitted, language='French', text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english (the CPC-12 authors' own English parallel version). No machine translation was produced. (4) OPTIONS: the paper publishes only the two anchors, 1='strongly disagree' and 7='strongly agree'. Points 2-6 were left BLANK rather than padded with their own numbers. Direction confirmed against the data: all three items are positively worded, intercorrelate positively (.53-.64), correlate positively with every well-being scale (.24 to .47), and sit at 5.37-5.56 of 7 - consistent with 7=agree, not the reverse. The anchor strings are the article's English gloss of French anchors it never prints, i.e. the same fallback as the item text. (5) MAPPING - PARTIAL, and one route dissents. mapping_basis=paper_order: the IRW codes ARE the deposit's column names but that deposit has no labels, so SAE_k <-> CPC-12 item (9+k) is an order inference nothing states. Three routes computed from the CPC-12's own development samples all pick the shipped permutation out of the six possible (see verify_pellerin2020_cpc_selfefficacy.R): the age gradient (S3 r(item,age)=.160/.013/.068 for items 10/11/12 vs French .171/-.032/.100 at wave 0 and .154/-.058/.090 at wave 5; shipped map has SSE .0031 against a runner-up .0161, and .0055 against .0172), the endorsement marker (item 11 has the highest mean and lowest SD in both German samples, and SAE_2 is the highest-mean lowest-SD French item), and the emotion-criterion marker (item 12 correlates .294 with life satisfaction vs .092/.114 and -.401 with neuroticism vs -.270/-.221, and SAE_3 is the strongest well-being correlate in 6 of 6 French wave x criterion comparisons). BUT a fourth statistic does not replicate: both German samples make {item 11, item 12} the most correlated within-block pair (.559 in S2, .486 in S3) while the French data makes {SAE_2, SAE_3} the LEAST correlated pair (.525 vs .641 and .588). The only remap that would repair that puts item 10 at SAE_2, which the age and endorsement routes both refuse outright, so the shipped mapping stands - but the disagreement is why this is recorded PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED. (6) RIGHTS: not blocked. The CPC-12 wording is published in full in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE appendix by its own developers, who built it as an open alternative to the licensed PCQ. The upstream originator of these three items is Schwarzer & Jerusalem's General Self-Efficacy Scale, and its own FAQ reserves no right: 'You do not need our explicit permission to utilize the scale in your research studies. We hereby grant you permission to use and reproduce the General Self-Efficacy Scale for your study, given that appropriate recognition of the source of the scale is made in the write-up of your study.' (https://userpage.fu-berlin.de/~health/faq_gse.pdf, sha256 fdc6c30d241f23e01ca05ac154edc0c5a75d6c51863d71715ce246afb277884f, fetched 2026-09-10; the scale's home page https://userpage.fu-berlin.de/~health/engscal.htm, sha256 d55e9c0046919ba4d4fe70f3a6099c1e1ecb0952eed256d6a21455a5e23f7b7c, states no fee, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term either). That is a grant with an attribution condition, not a reserved right, so it does not fire the irw#1945 test. instrument_rights_register.csv carries no CPC-12, PsyCap or General Self-Efficacy Scale row as of 2026-09-10. RETRY TEST: not applicable - the table shipped. The one thing left open is the administered French wording, and an unchanged retry would NOT recover it (determinate: neither the deposit nor the article published it); recovering it would need a French CPC-12 source located off-source, which is a later backfill pass rather than a retry.
public_note: The item text shipped for pellerin2020_cpc_selfefficacy is the CPC-12's published English (Lorenz et al., 2016, S1 Appendix), but the study was run in France and administered the scale in French; no French wording survives in the OSF deposit or the article, so the English is a stand-in for what respondents actually read, and the 1 = 'strongly disagree' / 7 = 'strongly agree' anchors are likewise the article's English gloss. The mapping of SAE_1/SAE_2/SAE_3 onto CPC-12 items 10/11/12 is inferred from the instrument's item order and checked against the CPC-12's own development samples: the age gradient (.171 / -.032 / .100 against the German .160 / .013 / .068), the endorsement marker (item 11 is the highest-mean, lowest-SD item in both German samples and SAE_2 is in the French data) and the well-being correlations (SAE_3 highest in 6 of 6 comparisons, matching item 12's emotional loading) all select this assignment out of the six possible, but the items' own intercorrelation ordering does not replicate - the German samples make items 11 and 12 the closest pair and here SAE_2 and SAE_3 are the furthest apart.

note: PASS with disclosures (batch_131). 42 rows = 6 items x 7 response levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes on both sets (GQ_1..GQ_6; resp 1-7). Live table is 6,060 rows, 1,010 per item (irw_table_sets aggregates; no full export was used for the gate). (1) INSTRUMENT (Step 3b). The live data IS the GQ-6. data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py melts exactly [f'GQ_{i}' for i in range(1,7)] out of the OSF file and names the GQ-6 in its comment; Pellerin & Raufaste (2020) Materials states 'The French version of the six-item Gratitude Questionnaire (GQ-6) was used to assess dispositional gratitude (McCullough et al., 2002; Shankland and Martin-Krumm, 2012)' and quotes two of its items ('I have so much in life to be thankful for,' 'I am grateful to a wide variety of people') - GQ-6 items 1 and 4 verbatim; the live 1-7 range matches both the paper's stated uniform 1='strongly disagree' to 7='strongly agree' format and the GQ-6's own scale; and re-running the authors' own reliability line, alpha(dat0[grep('GQ_',...)],check.keys=TRUE) under their exact exclusions (non-France, single-response, minor, gender='other'; n=470 at wave 0), returns alpha = 0.79, which is the figure the paper prints for gratitude toward the world, with keys c(+,+,-,+,+,-). No mismatch, and no other instrument in the battery has 6 items on 1-7. (2) TEXT SOURCE. The OSF deposit (osf.io/45aq3) holds only PsyR_lockdown2020.R and data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv; the CSV is a bare header row (GQ_1..GQ_6 among Hope_*, Opt_*, Cog_*, ...) with no variable or value labels, and the .R is an lme4/lmerTest analysis script containing no item strings. The Frontiers article has no supplementary material and reproduces only the two example items above. So the wording ships from the instrument's own published form: McCullough, Emmons & Tsang (2002) 'The grateful disposition', J Pers Soc Psychol 82(1):112-127, Appendix A, as distributed in full by the first author at pages.ucsd.edu/~memccullough/gratitude/GQ-6-scoring-interp.pdf, transcribed verbatim including terminal periods. One deliberate normalisation: the source PDF renders item 3 with a typographic apostrophe ('don’t'); the shipped string uses the ASCII apostrophe. Item 5 is shipped as the author's own form has it, 'more able to appreciate'; note that some validation papers (e.g. the Chilean one, PMC4815209) reprint it as 'better able to appreciate'. (3) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK. The study administered the French GQ-6 of Shankland & Martin-Krumm (2012, Pratiques Psychologiques 18(2):171-187) to a French sample. That French wording is NOT recoverable in scope: it is in neither the OSF deposit (both files checked; no French item text, only codes) nor the paper or its supplements (there are none). So the documented fallback applies - English in the base fields, the _translated columns omitted entirely, language='French', text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english (McCullough et al.'s own English for the same numbered items). No machine translation was produced. Shankland & Martin-Krumm is a paywalled Elsevier article and was not consulted; recovering the administered French is a later backfill, not part of this pass. (4) OPTIONS. All seven points carry a label because the instrument's own published form labels all seven (1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = slightly disagree, 4 = neutral, 5 = slightly agree, 6 = agree, 7 = strongly agree). CAVEAT, disclosed in the public_note: the study prints only its two endpoints (1 = 'strongly disagree' to 7 = 'strongly agree', which match the instrument's), so the five intermediate labels are the instrument's, not evidence about what the French form showed. Nothing was padded with its own number. Direction confirmed against the data: the four positively worded items sit at 4.90-5.54 of 7 and the two negatively worded ones at 3.19 and 3.38, and reverse-keying items 3 and 6 lifts raw alpha from 0.14 to 0.81 - consistent with 7 = agree, not the reverse. (5) INSTRUCTIONS deliberately blank. The study publishes none, and the instrument's own instruction ('Using the scale below as a guide, write a number beside each statement...') describes a paper-and-pencil administration that this online survey did not use, so shipping it would have been a false claim about what respondents read. correct_response blank (attitude scale, no key). section_id is the trivial single value with no section_prompt. (6) MAPPING. mapping_basis=paper_order, Step 5b status PARTIAL. The IRW codes ARE the deposit's column names (code-derivation pattern 1), but the deposit has no labels, so the tie GQ_k <-> GQ-6 item k is a number-to-number order inference that nothing states. Two checks constrain it, both in verify_pellerin2020_gq6.R: (A) the deposit's own derived Grat.world column is reproduced to 3.6e-15 by the 6-item mean with exactly columns 3 and 6 reversed, and by none of the other 63 reversal subsets (next-best deviation 1.17), which fixes {GQ_3,GQ_6} as the reverse pair - and the canonical GQ-6's reverse pair is items 3 and 6, sitting at exactly those positions; (B) on the live table GQ_3 and GQ_6 are the only two items with a negative mean correlation to the rest, GQ_6 has by far the weakest keyed loading (0.436 vs 0.650-0.875), matching item 6's documented status as the GQ-6's weak item (loading .079 in the Chilean adult EFA, PMC4815209 Table 1; 0.29 in the German validation, PMC7586006; .52 in the Brazilian one - it is the item dropped to form the GQ-5), and GQ_1/GQ_2 are the two strongest (0.850/0.875), matching items 1 and 2 as the near-synonymous top-loading pair (.838/.812). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: GQ_1 vs GQ_2 and GQ_4 vs GQ_5. Both checks act on blocks, and no published per-item statistic orders those pairs reproducibly - the Chilean EFA puts item 5 (.749) above item 4 (.701) while the live data puts them the other way round (0.650 vs 0.742), and the 'As I get older' item shows no age gradient here to mark it (partial r with age, controlling the scale total, is +0.022 for GQ_5 against +0.026 for GQ_2). Those two within-block orderings rest on the columns being numbered in the instrument's own order, which every checkable point is consistent with and none contradicts. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. (7) RIGHTS. Not blocked, and no caution to quote. The GQ-6's own first author distributes the complete six-item form with its scoring key and norms as a public PDF (pages.ucsd.edu/~memccullough/gratitude/GQ-6-scoring-interp.pdf) and the Penn Positive Psychology Center posts it for researchers (ppc.sas.upenn.edu/resources/questionnaires-researchers/gratitude-questionnaire); neither page, nor any other page located, states a fee, a permission requirement, a non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term. No restriction could be found and therefore none can be quoted, so under the standing rule silence is permission. instrument_rights_register.csv carries no GQ-6, gratitude or McCullough row as of 2026-09-10 (43 instruments); no row was added, to avoid a write race with the sibling agent in this round. RETRY TEST: not applicable - this is a clean pass, not a block. The one thing left open is the administered French wording, and an unchanged retry would NOT recover it (determinate: neither the deposit nor the article published it); that needs the paywalled Shankland & Martin-Krumm 2012 article, i.e. a later backfill, not a retry.
